newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thornton cuts Hong Kong weighting, favours Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Thornton cuts Hong Kong weighting, favours Jakarta.

text.p: Thornton Management (Asia) Ltd said on Monday that it has reduced its weighting in the Hong Kong stock market to about 35 percent of its US$1.5 billion Asia-ex-Japan portfolio from about 40 percent.
"China eased credit, the property market was rising and we had Wall Street going up. The amalgamation of those things (helped) Hong Kong," said joint managing director Chris Day.

"The credit easing is still there, but the government is intervening in the property market and Wall Street's stopped dead in its tracks. So it's not surprising Hong Kong has stopped dead as well," he said.
The portfolio has been reweighted in favour of Indonesia's Jakarta Stock Exchange, where a declining interest rate environment had created a positive near-term outlook, Day said.
"We're back up to a full weighting of about seven percent from about half that," Day said.
